userStories.title: Fix /404 direct-request 500 error and add noindex
userStories.description: As a search engine crawler, I need /404 to return a proper 404 status instead of erroring, and to be told not to index it.
acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce the bug first: a direct request to /404 currently returns HTTP 500 with an empty body, while requesting a genuinely nonexistent path (e.g. /this-does-not-exist) correctly returns 404 via the automatic fallback - fix src/pages/404.astro so BOTH cases render the same working 404 UI without a 500
Add <meta name="robots" content="noindex"> to the error page (currently missing)
curl -I on both the literal /404 path and a nonexistent path return 404 status, not 500, with identical rendered content
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Root cause traced in installed astro/@astrojs/node source: with output:'server', a prerendered 404.astro has no SSR page module, so a direct /404 request hits Astro's node adapter's render() with routeData already resolved (matched via allowPrerenderedRoutes) and skips the disk-fallback branch (its statusURL equals the request URL), then throws on the missing SSR module and returns an empty 500 - while a genuinely missing path takes the disk-read fallback branch and succeeds, explaining the split behavior. Fix: removed `export const prerender = true` from src/pages/404.astro so it renders on-demand for both cases, and added a `noindex` prop to Layout.astro (defaults false; renders `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` when true) wired up on the 404 page. Verified via npm run build (succeeds), code-level trace of node_modules/astro/dist/core/app/index.js + @astrojs/node/dist/serve-app.js, and a live curl check (run interactively afterward, since the autonomous run couldn't start a server without tool-approval): literal /404 -> 404, genuinely missing path -> 404, homepage control -> 200, noindex present on both 404 responses, bodies identical apart from per-request Clerk widget DOM ids (expected). npm run lint and npx tsc --noEmit -p . show only pre-existing errors in unrelated files, none new.

userStories.title: Guard CUSTOM_DOMAIN localhost fallback at production build time
userStories.description: As a developer deploying to Coolify, I need the build to fail loudly if CUSTOM_DOMAIN is misconfigured, instead of silently shipping canonical/OG/RSS URLs pointing at localhost.
acceptanceCriteria: In astro.config.mjs's getSite(), before falling through to the http://localhost:4321 return, add a check that throws a clear error naming the missing env var when none of CUSTOM_DOMAIN, VERCEL_URL, or CF_PAGES_URL are set AND the build is running in production mode

Confirm which env var reliably signals a production build at config-evaluation time in this Astro version (import.meta.env.PROD may not be populated this early - verify empirically, e.g. by logging process.env.NODE_ENV during a real npm run build) and gate on that
npm run dev continues to work unaffected with no env vars set (must not throw)
A production build (npm run build) with no CUSTOM_DOMAIN/VERCEL_URL/CF_PAGES_URL set throws a clear, actionable error instead of silently succeeding
A production build with CUSTOM_DOMAIN set succeeds normally
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: In astro.config.mjs's getSite(), added a throw before the localhost:4321 fallback, gated on process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' (empirically confirmed via a temporary debug log: astro build sets NODE_ENV=production, astro dev sets development, at config-evaluation time - import.meta.env.PROD is not usable this early) with an ALLOW_LOCALHOST_SITE_URL opt-out for legitimate local test builds, per the PRD's flagged risk that plain local `npm run build` (no CUSTOM_DOMAIN set, as used to verify US-001/US-002) is a real workflow. Verified live: `npm run dev` with no env vars starts cleanly; `npm run build` with no CUSTOM_DOMAIN/VERCEL_URL/CF_PAGES_URL throws the clear error and fails the build; `CUSTOM_DOMAIN=ligadu.com npm run build` succeeds normally. npm run lint and npx tsc --noEmit -p . show only pre-existing errors in unrelated files, none new.

userStories.title: Add security response headers via middleware (HSTS, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, CSP Report-Only)
userStories.description: As a security-conscious site owner, I need standard security headers on every response, with CSP staged safely given how many third-party origins this site depends on.
acceptanceCriteria: In src/middleware.ts, chain a new header-setting middleware with the existing clerkMiddleware() using Astro's sequence() - do not replace or break the existing Clerk auth middleware

Every response includes enforcing headers: Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options (SAMEORIGIN unless you find evidence Ligadu pages need to be embeddable by another origin, in which case document why and skip it), Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin

Every response includes a Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only header (NOT an enforcing Content-Security-Policy - this is intentional, do not make it enforcing) built from the site's actual third-party origins found via grep across src/: Clerk's required domains (check @clerk/astro docs or Clerk dashboard for the exact frontend API / img domains), fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com, cdn.jsdelivr.net (KaTeX), pagead2.googlesyndication.com and related AdSense domains, www.googletagmanager.com, stats.ligadu.com (self-hosted Umami), and frame-src/img-src entries for embed platforms already used in the codebase (YouTube, Twitter/X, TikTok, Instagram, Pinterest, CodePen - grep src/components for the exact hostnames)

Manually smoke test after building: sign in and out via Clerk still works, a post with an embed still renders it, ads still render if configured, Umami script still loads - none of these should be blocked since the CSP is Report-Only
Typecheck passes
